podcast.title: What The Tech Podcast (AU)
podcast.tagline: Conversations from the frontier of Australian tech and AI

episodes.title: Getting Hired in AI
keyInsights: If everyone's CV becomes equally polished with AI help, applicant-tracking systems lose their signal — the bottleneck shifts back to the human decision-maker.
Hybrid roles (ML engineer, analytics engineer) have moved from rare to standard in just a few years.
What used to sit outside pure AI has quietly absorbed AI expectations — the titles haven't changed but the required skills have.
The best move for candidates right now is treating AI fluency as a layer on top of their existing craft, not a replacement for it.
episodes.standoutMoment: The paradox of AI-assisted job applications: better CVs for everyone means less differentiation, not more.

episodes.title: Inside AI Coding Tools

guest.name: Monmayuri Bantler
guest.role: AI Engineering Leader (formerly GitLab, now Code Rabbit)

keyInsights: From an economic lens, machine learning and AI are both simply driving down the cost of prediction.
Code completion, generation and review are among the most impactful early generative-AI applications — not chatbots.
The real productivity gain isn't replacing the developer — it's removing the hours spent Googling small frustrations.
Evaluating whether coding assistants actually help is its own discipline, and harder than building them.
episodes.standoutMoment: Framing AI not as a creative tool but as an eraser of mundane friction — Googling, email polish, context switching.

episodes.title: AI Regulation & the EU AI Act
keyInsights: The EU is meaningfully ahead of Australia on AI regulation — and this is a wake-up call, not a far-future concern.
AI isn't a fad like crypto or the metaverse — it's becoming infrastructure, and regulators need to treat it that way.
Transformers were being explored by practitioners seven or eight years ago — today's attention is the tail end of a long curve.
Policy-makers who dismiss AI as passing hype are leaving their economies exposed to rules written elsewhere.
episodes.standoutMoment: A direct message to listening politicians: this isn't going away — deal with it.

episodes.title: Securing the AI Era
keyInsights: Traditional security was gated by heavy credentials; generative AI makes a frontier tool accessible in one browser tab.
Easy access hides complexity — the risk isn't malice, it's everyday users not knowing what the toy can or can't do.
Security paranoia paired with architecture thinking is a surprisingly effective combination for getting things built safely.
The education gap is the real vulnerability: people need to be taught the downsides of cuddly new technology.
episodes.standoutMoment: The "capable toy that can explode" metaphor — a vivid image for why accessibility without guardrails is risky.

episodes.title: Leadership Mindset in the AI Era
keyInsights: It's irresponsible for a leader today not to be thinking seriously about AI — it will reshape every organisation.
If you're not doing AI, your competitor is — and you had the chance to lead instead.
The reskilling numbers coming at us by 2030 aren't incremental — they're reshaping whole economies.
AI transformation is ultimately about humans — technology is just the catalyst.
episodes.standoutMoment: Leadership framed not as "choose AI" but as a duty of care: your people need you to have a view.

episodes.title: Product Management in the AI Era
keyInsights: AI product-market fit arrives like a wave, not a curve — zero to ten thousand users in weeks, not quarters.
A research paper published on Tuesday can be a startup product by Friday — AI PMs have to read the papers.
The line between technical and non-technical PM has collapsed; vibe coding is now part of the interview.
Creativity is king — the real differentiator is curiosity, cross-domain thinking, and a willingness to play.
Keep friends outside of AI — echo chambers are the fastest way to miss what users actually want.
episodes.standoutMoment: If your CEO is shipping features with AI on weekends and you can't, the gap isn't a tooling problem — it's a curiosity problem.

episodes.title: AI Governance & Cross-Functional Teams
keyInsights: Governance starts with principles, then structure, then process — in that order, not the other way around.
AI is software engineering with non-deterministic outputs — which means every existing function needs to relearn its role.
Cross-functional governance begins with executive sponsorship: someone has to own why we're doing this at all.
Governance is always evolving — accepting incompleteness is more realistic than waiting for a finished framework.
The legacy-vs-AI-native decision is now a strategic question: incrementally retrofit, or rebuild from scratch.
episodes.standoutMoment: The sports analogy — knowing the rules lets you play with confidence inside the boundaries, and spot the openings.

episodes.title: The Evolution of Data Engineering
keyInsights: Data engineering has shifted from "data janitors" to data product owners — reactive to proactive.
Unstructured data was always there; we just didn't have the tools to capture it. Now we do — and the volume is exponential.
The fundamentals haven't changed — SQL, data modelling, system design. The tooling has, and it keeps changing.
The next frontier is context engineering — orchestrating AI agents, not just crafting prompts.
Data migration as a discipline may disappear — why move data at all if the compute can come to it?
episodes.standoutMoment: A prediction: data migration as we know it won't exist in a few years — it's a transitional artefact, like horseshoes.

episodes.title: Building Australian AI from Scratch
keyInsights: AI should handle the cognitive load humans don't enjoy, freeing people to do what computers can't.
Australian-made AI isn't just about sovereignty — it's about laying a foundation for grassroots tech for generations to come.
Scarcity breeds better solutions: resource-constrained teams consistently outperform well-funded ones.
"For humans" is the first principle — not AGI, not ASI, not superintelligence as a north star.
episodes.standoutMoment: The Matilda naming story — evoking Banjo Paterson and the spirit of packing a swag to explore the frontier.

episodes.title: Designing AI at Massive Scale
keyInsights: Design is the journey from problem to solution — not the polish at the end.
Polished AI outputs can bypass the thinking that actually makes solutions right for the people using them.
Scaling AI design for hundreds of millions of users means designing for many simultaneous realities at once.
Good design today demands defining the problem more carefully than ever — not less.
episodes.standoutMoment: Reframing design as a problem-finding discipline rather than a solution-polishing one in the age of generative AI.

episodes.title: AI Capability, Robotics and Women in STEM
keyInsights: AI adoption in Australia is still nascent outside financial services — most sectors are still working out what it means.
Robotics already has mature safety and accountability frameworks that non-physical AI can learn from.
Australian AI and robotics startups begin with roughly ten times less capital than US equivalents.
Under 10% of expert opinions in the media come from women — shaping what the next generation believes is possible.
Australia needs real AI infrastructure — GPUs, yes, but also funding to build models on our own valuable datasets.
episodes.standoutMoment: The Neo robot critique — paying tens of thousands for a tele-operated robot that invites a stranger into your home as free training data.
